trigger: an operator or supervised-tier caller sends MCP delete_tag with a key over 64 bytes or with a byte below 0x20 and no approval_id; the generic C8 mint (mcp_server.cpp ~10310-10325) floors agent_id only, binds canonical_args(args) (which holds the raw key) as the ticket subject and stores the pending approval (submit_typed ~11190); the key floor at :25272 runs only when the approved ticket is redeemed
summary: The tag key reaches a stored approval ticket subject before the floor. The audit rows are clean (the pending row carries only agent_id and the approval id), control bytes are JSON-escaped by dump(), and size is bounded by the body cap, so this is not the audit-target_id defect g3-sec-1 named. Consequence: an approver can approve a ticket that is consumed and then refused with -32602, and mcp.md's redeem-time sentence is the only disclosure. set_tag is not approval-gated (requires_approval covers Tag Delete only), so only delete_tag is affected. Reviewers differed on the band: security-guardian derived LOW/pre-existing, unhappy-path and consistency-auditor MEDIUM or higher on an audit-integrity reading. Derived here: the audit control holds, so I1 does not apply; I8 only, LOW. Provenance recorded introduced because it was contested. Recommended: call refuse_unsafe_tag_key in the mint block for tool_name delete_tag next to the agent_id floor (one line, plus a gated-tier test and a rewritten mcp.md sentence), or file it.
classification_rationale: the mint-time floor is absent for the key; no wrong audit outcome
